Exemption 4 of the FOIA protects "trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person [that is] privileged or confidential."

FOIA Exemption 5 (deliberative process privilege) applies to inter-agency or intra-agency records where, for instance, there is a work product that is in draft format or documents that contain deliberations between parties leading up to a decision.

Exemption 6 protects the privacy interest of individuals, whose substantial interest in personal identity protection outweighs any public interest link in disclosure of information that could be used to identify them.? In cases such as this, the disclosure of the enclosed records “would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.”? See e.g., Pierce v. U.S. Air Force, 512 F.3d 184, 191 (5th Cir. 2007) (“To qualify as a similar file under Exemption 6…the information need only ‘appl[y] to the individual.”)??

title: Sheriff's Department PROTECT Act Policies November 2026 (Barnstable County Sheriff's Office)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Sheriff's Department PROTECT Act Policies November 2026 (Barnstable County Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1. Sheriff’s Department policies, memos or other guidance  currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:
A. Fingerprint and other data sharing with the above-named federal entities,
B. Guidance or policies concerning when communication with federal immigration authorities is allowed. This includes policies concerning how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances. This also includes how and under what circumstances department employees are to document and respond to ICE detainer requests and other requests for information.

2. All Sheriff’s Department policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of sheriff department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies concerning the use of sheriff department parking lots, facility interior, or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.  

3. All training materials the Sheriff’s Department has developed, used or trained employees on from September 4, 2026 through October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026) regarding civil immigration enforcement, communication with federal immigration authorities, or the use of Sheriff’s department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Citizens for Juvenile Justice is an independent nonprofit organization working to reform youth serving systems statewide through Massachusetts. We engage in advocacy across the Commonwealth to ensure all youth are treated fairly and equitably regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, disability or immigration status. We plan to use these records to ensure that all people in Massachusetts, including youth, are adequately protected by law enforcement agencies regardless of real or perceived immigration status.  In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.
The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,
Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initiatives 
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org

title: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Yakima Police Department)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: WA ALPR: A: External Access Audit Logs (1/4) (Yakima Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All system audit logs, as natively maintained in your agency's systems or your vendor's systems, reflecting access to your agency's ALPR system or any system used to store, process, or query ALPR data (e.g., Axon Evidence.com, Flock Safety portal, Motorola/Vigilant), by users affiliated with any agency other than your agency.

2. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) or agency name associated with each external query of your agency's ALPR system.

3. All system audit logs, as natively maintained, reflecting the user identifier, badge number, or account name associated with each query of your agency's ALPR system, whether the querying user was internal or external to your agency.

4. All records identifying which external agencies are currently authorized to access, query, or receive data from your agency's ALPR system, including any configuration record, permissions list, access control list, or authorized-agency registry maintained in your ALPR platform.  If this information exists only as a display within a software interface, a screenshot, faithful reproduction, or export of that display to any available file format is an acceptable and required form of production.

Note on vendor-held records: In Rodriguez v. City of Stanwood & Sedro-Woolley (Skagit County Superior Court, Nov. 6, 2025), the court held that ALPR data held by a third-party SaaS vendor on behalf of a government agency is a public record subject to PRA disclosure. Vendor custody does not relieve your agency of its production obligation. Each request below that encompasses vendor-held records is made on this basis. Please retrieve and produce all responsive records held by your ALPR vendor(s) on your agency's behalf.

Note on record creation: I am seeking existing records only. I understand that no agency is required to create a new record in response to a PRA request. However, producing a screenshot or other faithful reproduction of an existing electronic display is not creating a new record — it is reproducing an existing one, in the same manner as photocopying or scanning a paper document. Agencies cannot evade their production obligation by characterizing screenshots of existing system displays as "new records."

I am requesting these records for research and public interest purposes, submitted through MuckRock, a nonprofit journalism platform. I request that your agency consider waiving any fees given that this request is submitted for research and public interest purposes and that electronic production of the requested records should entail minimal or no actual cost under RCW 42.56.120. For any anticipated costs, please notify me before incurring them so that I may prioritize or narrow the request. This notification requirement should not be construed as authorization to delay production of records for which no fee will be incurred pending resolution of fees for other records in this request

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Phil Mocek

Today’s installment of records contains a total of 35 records. The ALPR Hot List Management reports for the dates of 1/1/2025 through the date of your request; and, a variety of screenshots from Axon relating to various settings and user access. Lt. Cavin provided the following additional response during our attempts to find and access audit logs from Axon: As a matter of practice we did not run audits of the AXON system, since officers were rarely searching plates in
that system.  The AXON plate scans were feeding into the FLOCK system so there was no need to run a check in AXON since a FLOCK search would produce records in both systems. 
Regarding Vigilant, previously used for parking citations, Lt. Cavin has provided the following information: When the user docks their computer and logs into the Vigilant system, they drive through the parking lots and the ALPR scans license plates.  They then wait a specified amount of time 1-2 hours depending on the zone, and drive back through.  The system provides an alert through the program if they scan a license plate/vehicle in the same location (parking spot).  The operator then checks to see if the vehicle has a valid parking permit through the city permit system and determines if a citation is necessary. The data collected by the Vigilant ALPR is stored locally on the hard drive in the patrol vehicle, and is not uploaded to any server or system that would allow for searches. 
 
View it at https://records.yakimawa.gov/record-requests/view/2108156 (https://records.yakimawa.gov/record-requests/view/2108156)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CVISS Member Agencies - LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing Agreements (Elk Grove Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All MOUs, contracts, addendums, or other legal documents signed by your agency and LexisNexis (and subsidiaries, including LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, etc.). This may include (but is not limited to) a LexisNexis Consortium Sub-Agency Addendum, Schedule A, or other agreements.
2) Any MOUs or other agreements between your agency and CVISS or Sacramento County Sheriff related to sharing RMS/CAD data.
3) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

Context: We understand that CVISS moved to the LexisNexis Accurint platform to share data among CVISS member agencies. We are seeking to understand whether your agency and other CVISS members share contributed data with agencies beyond the consortium (e.g., the Public Safety Data Exchange / PSDEX national database), or whether data sharing is restricted to CVISS members only. Often LexisNexis Sub-Agency Addendums allow agencies to choose whether they share nationally or only within the consortium - we seek to understand what your agency chose to do.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

title: Granules Pharmaceuticals Inc., FEI 3011585184 — July 2022 and December 2023 Inspection Records and Corrective Actions

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Granules Pharmaceuticals Inc., FEI 3011585184 — July 2022 and December 2023 Inspection Records and Corrective Actions
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

FDA inspections of the following drug manufacturing establishment:

Firm: Granules Pharmaceuticals Inc.
FEI: 3011585184
Address: 3701 Concorde Parkway, Chantilly, VA 20151
Inspection end dates: July 22, 2022, and December 15, 2023
Program area: Human drug manufacturing / current good manufacturing practices (CGMP)

For each inspection, I request:

The final Establishment Inspection Report (EIR), including available exhibits, attachments, and inspectional findings.

The firm's written response to FDA Form 483, including initial responses, supplemental responses, and corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plans submitted to FDA.

Documentation submitted by the firm supporting implementation or completion of proposed corrective actions, including relevant root-cause analyses, revised procedures, investigation summaries, effectiveness checks, and supporting correspondence.

FDA's written evaluations or assessments of the firm's responses and proposed corrective actions, including records indicating whether the responses were considered adequate, inadequate, or in need of further verification.

Correspondence between FDA and Granules Pharmaceuticals concerning the cited deficiencies, corrective actions, implementation deadlines, follow-up inspections, and verification of corrective actions.

Final inspection classification records and associated classification memoranda, including any records explaining the basis for the final classification or subsequent compliance decisions.

For item 5, please search correspondence dated July 22, 2022, through December 31, 2024, relating to either inspection.

I am particularly interested in records concerning manufacturing controls, quality assurance, laboratory testing, investigations of deviations, and deficiencies potentially affecting extended-release pharmaceutical products.

Please provide all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive records. If any information is withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemption and provide sufficient information to describe the withheld material.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma Yasinski
